title: WebGL liquid hero background
description: A full-screen WebGL2 fragment shader that animates soft, drifting organic blobs (domain-warped fractal noise) with subtle mouse parallax. Captures the technique behind a shader-driven hero canvas without any 3D model or external library.

source.name: technique recreation inspired by landonorris.com hero (Off+Brand)

a11y: Honors prefers-reduced-motion: renders a single still frame and skips the animation loop.

title: Magnetic button
description: On hover the element translates a fraction (~0.35) of the cursor offset toward the pointer; an inner label lags further for depth. Springs home on leave.

source.name: common portfolio pattern (not on vanschneider.com homepage)

a11y: Pointer-only enhancement; ignored on touch / coarse pointers.

title: Springy pill button (background pops with overshoot)
description: A pill-shaped button whose rounded fill lives behind the label (absolute, inset:0, z-index:-1). On hover the fill scales up from center with a springy overshoot ease so it pops past its target and settles — a satisfying, tactile bounce. The label stays put; only the pill breathes.

params.ease: cubic-bezier(0.17, 0.67, 0.3, 1.33)  (overshoots — the >1 final control point is the bounce)

a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: the pill still fills on hover but with a plain, non-overshooting ease and no bounce.

title: Directional underline wipe
description: Pure CSS. An underline scales in from the left on hover and out to the right on leave via a scaleX + transform-origin swap.
a11y: Decorative; underline is supplementary to the link text.

title: Hover-to-reveal index (image trails cursor)
description: A text link list where hovering a row fades in a shared image that swaps its src per row and trails the cursor with inertia (lerp).
a11y: Pointer-only enhancement; the list links work without it.

title: Sticky nav that tints on scroll
description: A position:fixed bar that fades a background/blur in once the user scrolls past a threshold. transition: background-color 0.2s linear.
a11y: No motion concerns; purely a color/opacity change.

title: Scroll velocity skew (momentum lean)
description: The momentum cue paired with Lenis-style smooth scroll on landonorris.com: content skews and stretches a touch in the direction of travel based on scroll velocity, then springs back to flat when motion stops. Velocity is smoothed with a lerp so it feels weighted, not jittery. Great layered over the smooth-scroll effect.
a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: no skew/scale, content stays flat.

title: Smooth / inertia scroll (the Lenis feel)
description: Eases the page toward the real scroll position for a weighted, inertial feel. Hand-rolled vanilla version to show the mechanism, plus the drop-in Lenis snippet for production.
a11y: Honor prefers-reduced-motion: skip smoothing, use native scroll.

title: Clip-path wipe (image loads in from an edge)
description: The element stays fully opaque while a clip-path polygon grows from one edge (left, right, top, or bottom). The 'pictures that load from left to right' effect. No inner-image scale — a pure mask wipe.

title: Scroll parallax (layered media depth)
description: The landonorris.com depth move: full-bleed media sits in a fixed-aspect frame and its inner image (plus foreground/caption layers) translate at different speeds as the frame crosses the viewport, so foreground lags and background drifts. Speed per layer via data-speed; driven by a single rAF loop reading each frame's progress.
a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: no parallax, layers stay put.

title: Scroll reveal (fade · rise · skew · 3D tilt · blur)
description: The signature vanschneider.com move: as a block enters view it fades in while rising, skewing slightly, and rotating in 3D (and optionally un-blurring), over a slow 2-4s Power ease. Variants change the from-state per block.

title: Scroll scale reveal (clip + zoom on enter)
description: The landonorris.com media entrance: as a block scrolls up into view its clip-path inset opens from a narrow slit to full frame while the inner image eases down from an overscale, so the picture seems to 'unmask' and settle. Scrubbed to scroll progress (not a one-shot) so it tracks the scrollbar.

title: Scroll-to-fly 3D project space (camera flythrough)
description: Scroll flies a camera through project cards scattered along a 3-turn spiral in CSS 3D space. Depth wraps infinitely, cards fade in from the deep and out past the lens, a starfield stretches on the z-axis with velocity for warp streaks, the whole world tilts with the mouse, and perspective tightens as you accelerate. A HUD reads out velocity and camera z.

params.scatter: angle = i/count * PI*6; x = cos*26vw, y = sin*24vh; rotZ = ±7deg random
params.fade: in over z -3000→-2000, out over z 100→500, wrap at count*zGap
params.warp: perspective = 1000 - min(|vel|*6, 600); star scale3d(1,1, 1+|vel|*0.12 clamped to 10)
params.hover: rect hit-test +22px margin, nearest card lerps +50px toward camera at 0.12

a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: no flight — wheel hijack, starfield and tilt are skipped and cards render as a static scrollable grid.

title: Scroll paper peel (corner folds flat as you scroll)
description: The trevornoah.com hero peel: a square 'page' folds its top-right corner over along a diagonal crease as you scroll. It is a FLAT fold, not a 3D rotation — the flap is the page content clipped to the corner triangle and reflected across the crease (matrix(0,1,1,0,0,0) mirror about the top-left origin, then translated so the crease endpoints stay pinned), so it reads as the mirrored underside of the paper. A second layer shows through the cut. Scrubbed to scroll position, so scrolling down folds and scrolling back up un-folds — the fold tracks scroll direction.

params.front_clip: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - L) 0, 100% L, 100% 100%, 0 100%)  — removes the top-right triangle
params.flap_clip: polygon(calc(100% - L) 0, 100% 0, 100% L)  — the removed triangle, clipped in local space
params.flap_transform: translate(calc(100% - L), calc(L - 100%)) matrix(0,1,1,0,0,0)  — reflect across the diagonal crease, endpoints pinned
params.L: calc(--p * 100%)  (page is square so % maps to a true 45deg crease)
params.progress: --p 0..1 scrubbed from how far the sticky stage has scrolled through its own height, eased in-out
params.note: The site's peeled layer is a flat matrix3d mirror with preserve-3d; the fold mechanism (clip + reflected back + diagonal crease) is verified from the live DOM. The exact scroll-to-progress curve is a clean reconstruction — the site drives it via Webflow IX2 which didn't expose per-scroll keyframes to scripting.

a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: no scrubbing — the page is shown flat and fully readable, the flap is hidden and the section collapses to normal flow.

title: Pinned scroll section (sticky + horizontal track)
description: The landonorris.com chapter move: a section pins to the viewport (position:sticky) while a tall outer track scrolls past, and that scroll distance is mapped to a horizontal translate of an inner row — so vertical scrolling scrubs through panels left-to-right. Progress also drives a thin progress bar. CSS sticky does the pin; JS only maps progress to transform.
a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: track unpins and panels stack vertically (native scroll).

title: Reveal on scroll (CSS transition + stagger)
description: Lightweight reveal: elements start translated + transparent and animate in via CSS transition when they enter view (IntersectionObserver, one-shot). Per-element --d delay variable produces staggers. Minimal-JS alternative to the WAAPI scroll-reveal.

title: Marquee with scroll-velocity surge
description: An infinite horizontal ticker that drifts on a rAF loop and surges faster the quicker you scroll (scroll-velocity coupling). Track is duplicated for a seamless loop.
